note.simple: This end is the 'acid' in lactic acid. It can join to the OH end of another lactic acid.
note.deeper: A carboxylic acid. When it reacts with an alcohol (OH) the two lose a water molecule and form an ester link: that is how lactic acid units join into PLA.

note.simple: The other joining point. An OH on one lactic acid meets the acid end of the next.
note.deeper: A secondary alcohol on the chiral carbon. Lactic acid is a hydroxy acid: it carries both halves of an ester on the same small molecule.

note.simple: This carbon holds four different things, so lactic acid comes in a left-handed and a right-handed form, like gloves. Bacteria can make almost pure left-handed (L) lactic acid.
note.deeper: The stereocentre is (S) in L-lactic acid. Microbial fermentation can give up to 99.9% L; the ratio of L to D units in PLA largely controls how much of it can crystallise.
